definition: Behaviour that appears without being trained for directly, which the sources treat as both the appeal and the reliability problem of outcome-based RL. One argues the reasoning behaviours RL elicits incidentally are unpredictable in timing and consistency, and replaces them with explicit alignment to logical primitives. Another reports emergence in an adversarial setting, where a trained planner discovers decoy avoidance and adaptive state prioritization that static heuristics never produce. A survey organizes such findings under unintended behaviours alongside training dynamics and reasoning mechanisms. The shared position is that emergence is real and that relying on it is a design weakness.

evidence.note: An agentic RLVR red-teaming framework that trains an LLM planner to attack deep-RL cyber-defence agents, showing those defences were only ever evaluated against static attackers.
evidence.title: Trident : How to Break Deep Reinforcement Learning Cyber Defenses (Agentic)

evidence.note: A survey organizing mechanistic findings about reasoning models into training dynamics, reasoning mechanisms and unintended behaviours, and arguing the field needs a unified theoretical framework.
evidence.title: Towards a Mechanistic Understanding of Large Reasoning Models: A Survey of Training, Inference, and Failures

evidence.note: Replaces reliance on unpredictable emergent 'aha moments' by explicitly aligning models to deduction, induction and abduction on self-verifiable tasks before domain RL.
evidence.title: Beyond 'Aha!': Toward Systematic Meta-Abilities Alignment in Large Reasoning Models

name: emergent behaviour
